newsitem.title: CHINA: China executes man in Jack the Ripper type slayings.
newsitem.headline: China executes man in Jack the Ripper type slayings.

text.p: China has executed a man convicted of murdering 10 women in a string of Jack the Ripper type killings.
Zhao Gengyun, 31, was put to death on July 17 after the Yunnan provincial Higher People's Court rejected his appeal, the Nanjing Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Monday.
It gave no reason for the delay in reporting the execution in the southwestern province of Yunnan.
The unemployed Zhao was arrested on June 6 and convicted of killing 10 prostitutes in the lakeside town of Dali between May 1994 and May 1996, the newspaper said.

Zhao told police that he slashed or strangled the women in revenge for being jilted by a lover. He also said he had contracted venereal disease after having sex with one of the women and others had stolen money from him.
Another woman managed to escape from Zhao after being attacked. She erroneously identified the man's brother as her assailant but police eventually concluded it was Zhao.
Before Zhao's arrest ended the killing spree, few women dared to walk the streets of Dali alone in the evening, the newspaper said.
The infamous Jack the Ripper stalked the streets of London, murdering prostitutes, in the late 1800s. He was never caught.
